name: Srodmiescie
tagline: The rebuilt centre, between the station and the culture zone
description: Katowice's core, remade over the last fifteen years around the market square, the pedestrianised Mariacka bar street and the walk north to the concert hall. Flats range from restored tenements to modern blocks. This is where the city's transformation is most visible and where almost everything is walkable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the bars, the concert hall and the station all on foot
pros: Mariacka street's bars and restaurants at the door
Walking distance to the culture zone and the main station
Best fibre coverage and the most coworking options
cons: Weekend noise on and around Mariacka
Rents are the highest in the city
Traffic on the arteries that cut through the centre

name: Koszutka
tagline: Just north of the centre, quieter and close to the concert hall
description: A residential district immediately north of the railway, within easy walking distance of the culture zone with its concert hall, museum and congress centre. Mid-century blocks with green between them, a local market and everyday shops. It trades a little atmosphere for considerably lower rents than the centre.
bestFor: Working stays that want quiet at night and the centre ten minutes away
pros: Ten to fifteen minutes on foot to the culture zone
Local shops, market and green space
cons: Little in the way of bars or restaurants
Blocks are plain and some are tired
The railway cutting separates it from the centre

name: Osiedle Paderewskiego
tagline: Modernist towers set in a park, five minutes from the centre
description: A 1970s estate of tall slabs laid out inside a large park on the eastern edge of the centre, next to the valley of three ponds. It is architecturally striking in a way that divides people, but the flats are large, the green space is real and the walk into town is short.
bestFor: People who want space, trees and a short walk into the centre
pros: Surrounded by park and the ponds valley
Ten-minute walk to the market square
cons: Few shops or cafes inside the estate
Lifts and services vary by block

name: Ligota
tagline: The student and hospital district, cheapest rents in the city
description: A southwestern district built around the medical university and its hospitals, with its own railway station and a student population that keeps prices low. Low blocks, allotments and the Katowice forest belt on the southern side. It feels like a separate small town attached to the city.
bestFor: Long stays on the tightest budget, with forest running instead of nightlife
pros: Forest belt for running and cycling on the doorstep
Own train station, ten minutes to the centre
cons: Nothing much happens here in the evening
Feels detached from the rest of the city

name: Nikiszowiec
tagline: A preserved red-brick miners' settlement, unlike anywhere else in Poland
description: A complete workers' colony built between 1908 and 1918 in red brick around interlinked courtyards, still lived in and now protected as a historic monument. It is a genuine curiosity and increasingly a weekend destination, with a few cafes and a market square. Living here means a bus into town.
bestFor: A stay somewhere genuinely unusual, with a commute traded for character
pros: Architecture with no real equivalent anywhere in the country
Weekend cafes and a small market
cons: Twenty-five minutes by bus to the centre
